CPVT is highly likely given its hallmark presentation of adrenergically triggered polymorphic VT or bidirectional VT during exercise, often with normal resting ECG and no structural abnormalities. LQTS (especially LQT1) is also highly plausible, as it commonly manifests with syncope or arrest during exertion or emotion due to Torsades de Pointes. HCM remains a leading cause of sudden cardiac death in young athletes, typically presenting with exertional syncope or arrest due to ventricular arrhythmias or outflow obstruction. ARVC should be considered given its association with exercise-induced ventricular arrhythmias and structural substrate (fibrofatty replacement), though diagnosis often requires advanced imaging or genetic testing. WPW is less common but can precipitate sudden collapse if AF conducts rapidly over an accessory pathway; however, it usually presents earlier and may show preexcitation on baseline ECG—making it somewhat less likely without corroborating ECG evidence. Absence of trauma rules out commotio cordis, and lack of febrile history makes myocarditis less probable as an acute trigger."}
